title: OpenAI ChatCompletions metadata-preservation proxy
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Create a compatibility proxy that accepts OpenAI ChatCompletions v1 requests and preserves as much request/response metadata as possible while mapping to Redwood's internal streaming and structured-output model. The goal is to avoid information loss for customers migrating from OpenAI endpoints: preserve user-provided ids, role attributes, message-level metadata (e.g., client_timestamp, conversation_id), and function_call hints; ensure deterministic mapping for stream frames, tool/function calling sequences, and fallback to Redwood normalized structured-output events. This ticket implements the translation rules, streaming event framing, idempotency token handling, and integration tests for reorder/partial delivery scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy accepts OpenAI ChatCompletions v1 POST and responds with a 200 for valid payloads, mapping to Redwood request model without dropping metadata fields.

Streaming: each OpenAI SSE event (data: ...) is translated into the Redwood stream envelope types: partial_choice, tool_call_start, tool_call_chunk, tool_call_end, final_choice, and meta_patch. Event order and reconstructions must match spec and pass e2e reorder tests.

Function/tool calling: OpenAI function_call objects are deterministically converted into Redwood toolInvocation events; function arguments are preserved and validated against the customer's declared JSON schema when present.

Idempotency: Idempotency-key, x-request-id, and Redwood client_id are propagated and used to deduplicate retries; retry scenarios do not produce duplicated tool executions in Dedicated/Private deployments.

Metadata preservation: conversation_id, user.metadata, timestamps (client_sent_at), and any top-level 'model' tags are available in the resulting Redwood request object and visible in Console diagnostics.
Telemetry: mapping latency, dropped-fields count, and a mapping-fidelity score are emitted for each proxied request and surfaced on per-route dashboards.
Automated tests: property-based tests for stream fragmentation/reorder and integration test against the runtime with simulated tool execution (fake tool) pass in CI.
Design/UX: Console shows both the original incoming OA payload (read-only) and the normalized Redwood request in the request inspector; PM/Design signoff recorded in comments.
comments: 2026-02-28 - Ravi Patel: Initial spike complete. PoC demonstrates translating OA 'choices' stream into event envelopes without losing message-level metadata. PoC repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/oa-compat-proxy/tree/spike-metadata
2026-03-03 - Ava Thompson: Design QA - Confirmed we need to preserve arbitrary top-level fields under 'metadata' (customers rely on this for routing downstream). Added to acceptance criteria.

2026-03-05 - Zoe Martinez (PM): Please ensure Console shows the raw payload. UX should allow toggling the normalized view. Linking design spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COMP/Chat+Compatibility+Proxy+Design

2026-03-07 - Code review (ENG): PR opened with core mapping logic. Feedback from Jonas: wrap long-running tool calls in a cancellable context and add explicit partial-checkpoint events to resume on reconnection. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/oa-compat-proxy/pull/42

2026-03-09 - Engineering note: Implemented idempotency key propagation and dedupe layer. Added integration test that replays the same stream twice; second replay is a no-op for tool execution but still returns the normalized response to the client.
2026-03-11 - Security (Naomi): Need KMS tag propagation when customers include encrypted metadata in 'user' block. Marked security_review_required=true and opened securiy checklist ticket.

2026-03-12 - Testing: E2E harness updated to simulate TCP fragment drops and SSE reordering. Early run shows a subtle bug where a 'function_call' split across two SSE events loses the closing brace; fix applied by buffering until a complete JSON token is formed.
2026-03-14 - Ava Thompson: Moving to In Progress -> In Review soon. Preparing release notes draft and telemetry dashboard queries. Assigned final QA to SRE team for dedicated capacity testing.
decision_log: 2026-03-04 - Decision: Use explicit event types instead of embedding domain logic in 'choices' text. This allows deterministic reconciliation and improves observability.
2026-03-06 - Decision: Preserve unknown top-level fields under an opaque 'originalPayload' map exposed in Console; do not automatically index them for routing until customer opt-in is implemented.

2026-03-08 - Decision: For function_call arguments we will run a best-effort JSON schema validation if the function provides a schema; failures will result in a 'schema_mismatch' meta_patch event but will not silently drop the call.
2026-03-10 - Decision: Default behavior in Dedicated/Private is to forward tool execution requests to the customer-specified tool endpoint. For Hosted, run tool in a sandbox with explicit audit logs.
